spec.description: Edge traffic drilldown for lb2. Filter bar drives every panel; click pie slices and table rows to narrow down to the raw requests in the Logs row.

spec.expr: sum by (status_code) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` | label_format status_code="{{if .status_code}}{{.status_code}}{{else}}tcp{{end}}" [$__range]))

spec.description: Share of matching requests per exact HTTP status code (200, 304, 403…); TCP connections with no HTTP status are the 'tcp' slice. Click a slice to filter the whole dashboard. Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows.
spec.title: By HTTP status

spec.expr: sum by (method) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` | label_format method="{{if .method}}{{.method}}{{else}}tcp{{end}}" [$__range]))

spec.description: Share of matching requests per HTTP method (GET, POST…); TCP connections are the 'tcp' slice. Click a slice to filter the whole dashboard. Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows.
spec.title: By method

spec.expr: sum by (backend) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` [$__range]))

spec.description: Share of matching requests per backend (server pool) — the closest thing to a per-team/per-service split. Click a slice to filter the whole dashboard. Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows.
spec.title: By backend

spec.expr: sum by (server) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` [$__range]))

spec.description: Share of matching requests per individual server. <NOSRV> = request never reached a server. Click a slice to filter the whole dashboard. Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows.
spec.title: By server

spec.expr: sum by (frontend) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` [$__range]))

spec.description: Share of matching requests per entry point (which listener the traffic arrived on). A trailing ~ marks an SSL connection in HAProxy's log format. Click a slice to filter the whole dashboard. Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows.
spec.title: By frontend

spec.expr: sum by (termination) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` | label_format termination="{{if .termination}}{{.termination}}{{else}}n/a{{end}}" [$__range]))

spec.description: HOW each matching session ended (HAProxy termination flags). 1st char: - normal, C client abort, S server abort/refused, s server timeout, c client timeout, P blocked by proxy, R resource exhausted, I internal error. 2nd char: session state when it ended. 'n/a' = unparsed lines (e.g. SSL handshake failures). Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows.
spec.title: By termination code

spec.expr: topk(20, sum by (path_group) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` | label_format path_group=`{{if .path}}{{regexReplaceAll "\\?.*" .path ""}}{{else}}tcp (no path){{end}}` [$__range])))

spec.description: The 20 most-requested URL paths among matching requests, with ?query=strings stripped so all calls to one endpoint count together. 'tcp (no path)' = non-HTTP connections. Click a path to filter the dashboard to that path prefix. Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows. Very long ranges can hit Loki's max_query_series limit.
spec.title: Top paths (query strings stripped)

links.title: Filter dashboard to this path prefix

spec.expr: topk(20, sum by (client_ip) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` [$__range])))

spec.description: The 20 client IPs sending the most matching requests — heavy users, integrations, monitors or abusers. Click an IP to filter the whole dashboard to it. Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows.
spec.title: Top client IPs

spec.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` [$__range]))

spec.description: Every request lb2 logged and the filter bar matches — HTTP requests on all frontends plus TCP connections (xmpp, redis). Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows.
spec.title: Requests (range)

spec.expr: topk(30, sum by (server, client_ip) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` [$__range])))

spec.description: Which servers get the most hits from which IPs: the top 30 (client IP, server) combinations by matching requests. Click a row to filter to that pair, or to the IP alone. Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows.
spec.title: Server ↔ client IP (top pairs)

spec.expr: topk(20, sum by (client_ip) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` | status_code=~`[45]..` [$__range])))

spec.description: The 20 client IPs receiving the most error responses — broken clients, misconfigured integrations, or probing/attack traffic. Click an IP to filter the whole dashboard to it. Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows.
spec.title: Top IPs causing 4xx/5xx

spec.expr: haproxy_server_status{instance=~"$instance", proxy=~"$backend", server=~"$server"}

spec.description: Health-check verdict for every server slot in every backend, worst first (DOWN=red, UP=green, MAINT, DRAIN). A server appears once per backend it serves. Time range: shows the state at the END of the selected range (live state when the range ends at now); range length has no effect.
spec.title: Server status

spec.expr: haproxy_server_response_time_average_seconds{instance=~"$instance", proxy=~"$backend", server=~"$server"}

spec.description: How long each server takes to answer, as HAProxy sees it — a rolling MEAN of that server's last 1024 requests, not a percentile, so brief slow outliers are smoothed out. Only honors the instance/backend/server filters (log filters like status or path do not apply). Plotted across the selected range.
spec.title: Server response time (avg of last 1024 req)

spec.expr: haproxy_server_current_sessions{instance=~"$instance", proxy=~"$backend", server=~"$server"}

spec.description: Concurrently open connections per server at each scrape — a load/saturation gauge, not a request count. Only honors the instance/backend/server filters. Plotted across the selected range.
spec.title: Server current sessions

spec.expr: max by (proxy) (haproxy_frontend_status{instance=~"$instance"})
max by (proxy) (haproxy_frontend_current_sessions{instance=~"$instance"})
max by (proxy) (haproxy_frontend_max_sessions{instance=~"$instance"})

spec.description: Every configured frontend (listener) with its state, currently open sessions, and the highest session count seen since the last HAProxy restart. Time range: shows the state at the END of the selected range (live state when the range ends at now); range length has no effect.
spec.title: Frontends

spec.expr: max by (proxy) (haproxy_backend_status{instance=~"$instance"})
max by (proxy) (haproxy_backend_active_servers{instance=~"$instance"})
max by (proxy) (haproxy_backend_backup_servers{instance=~"$instance"})
max by (proxy) (haproxy_backend_current_sessions{instance=~"$instance"})
max by (proxy) (haproxy_backend_current_queue{instance=~"$instance"})

spec.description: Every configured backend (server pool) with its state, how many active/backup servers are healthy, currently open sessions, and queued requests waiting for a free server (queue > 0 means the pool is saturated). Busiest first. Time range: shows the state at the END of the selected range (live state when the range ends at now); range length has no effect.
spec.title: Backends

spec.expr: {job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path`

spec.description: The raw HAProxy log lines behind every number above, newest first — this is where every click-to-filter ultimately lands. Expand a line to see parsed fields (client IP, path, termination code, timing). Time range: only lines inside the selected range, capped at the newest 1000 — narrow the filters or range to see everything.
spec.title: Matching requests

spec.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` | status_code=~`[45]..` [$__range]))

spec.description: Matching requests that ended in an HTTP 4xx (client error) or 5xx (server error). Click the panel to filter the whole dashboard down to just these errors. Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows.
spec.title: Errors 4xx/5xx

spec.expr: count(sum by (client_ip) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` [$__range])))

spec.description: How many DISTINCT client IP addresses sent matching requests — a rough audience/attacker-diversity gauge, counted from structured metadata. Time range: aggregated over the ENTIRE selected range — widen the range and the number grows. Very long ranges can hit Loki's max_query_series limit.
spec.title: Unique client IPs

spec.expr: count(haproxy_frontend_status{instance=~"$instance", proxy!~"stats"} == 1)

spec.description: How many frontends (listening entry points: https-in, media_https, xmpp…) are OPEN and accepting traffic, excluding the stats page. Native HAProxy gauge. Time range: shows the state at the END of the selected range (live state when the range ends at now); range length has no effect.
spec.title: Active frontends

spec.expr: count(haproxy_backend_active_servers{instance=~"$instance", proxy!~"stats"} > 0)

spec.description: How many backends (server pools) currently have at least one healthy server to route to. A drop here means a whole pool lost all its servers. Native HAProxy gauge. Time range: shows the state at the END of the selected range (live state when the range ends at now); range length has no effect.
spec.title: Active backends

spec.expr: count(haproxy_server_status{instance=~"$instance"} == 1)

spec.description: Individual server slots passing health checks, summed across all backends (one physical server counts once per backend it serves). Compare with the Server status table in Health & inventory to see which are down. Time range: shows the state at the END of the selected range (live state when the range ends at now); range length has no effect.
spec.title: Servers UP

spec.expr: sum by (status_code) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` | label_format status_code="{{if .status_code}}{{.status_code}}{{else}}tcp{{end}}" [$__auto]))

spec.description: Matching request volume split by HTTP status code; TCP connections (no HTTP status) appear as 'tcp'. Watch for a 4xx/5xx band widening — that is an error spike. Time range: one point per auto-sized interval across the range — zooming in/out changes the bucket size, so absolute heights shift.
spec.title: Requests over time by status

spec.expr: sum by (server) (count_over_time({job="haproxy", instance=~"$instance", frontend=~"$frontend", backend=~"$backend", server=~"$server", method=~"$method", status_code=~"$status_code"} |~ `(?i)$search` | client_ip=~`$client_ip` | path=~`$path` [$__auto]))

spec.description: Matching request volume split by the backend server that handled each request. <NOSRV> = no server was picked (blocked, queued or failed before dispatch). Uneven bands can reveal load-balancing skew. Time range: one point per auto-sized interval across the range — zooming in/out changes the bucket size, so absolute heights shift.
spec.title: Requests over time by server
